models.qualification: Physical-object 3D capture published by the professional art foundry and scan-service provider gussbronze (GEBR Ihle Bildguss GmbH). The publisher’s 1920 px model thumbnail was inspected alongside the Alte Nationalgalerie photograph and matches Begas’s Pan Comforting Psyche composition, including hands, pipes, wings, hair, drapery and rounded base. The provider labels the model “begas berlin” but does not record the exact physical version, material, manufacture date, dimensions or capture method. Those fields must remain qualified, and the museum marble’s accession/date/measurements cannot be transferred to this unidentified version. Public model metadata identifies a non-AI upload and an original vertex-colored OBJ; this request obtains only the authenticated provider GLB delivery. Native review must inspect both crowns, wing edges, hands, goat hooves, reverse and base before acceptance. Preserve vertex colors and all authored appearance.

First-party Cleveland Museum of Art scan of accession 2000.6, a solid-cast Greek bronze dated 510–500 BCE and measuring 21.5 cm. The current museum page identifies the figure as Herakles and explicitly links this exact Sketchfab UID. The provider model retains its former title Statuette of an Athlete. The model’s largest reference was actually inspected and ROOT approved the adult muscular anatomy and body-theme fit. Missing hands, one arm and damaged feet are documented historical losses, rather than asserted capture defects. Mounting pins are visible below the feet and should remain documented. Native review must inspect the crown, remaining arm edges, feet, pins, reverse and underside. Preserve the provider’s mottled bronze appearance, maps and material. The museum measurement is documentary until the acquired model’s physical scale is verified.
